data.title: Saltire Capital
data.rumour: Saltire Capital sends someone politer. Their interest is the whole of Main Street.
about: A story about the new lender after the Gilded Hand. Lionel Shattuck, the cobbler three doors down, asks for a loan on his father's watch because Saltire Capital bought his mortgage and doubled his payments (§{salShattuck}). Then Imogen Thackeray of Saltire offers you a "partnership" in Harborside Commons, a glass-fronted redevelopment of Main Street (§{salThackeray}): sign, and your installments stop for good, but the building goes to Saltire at the end of the lease. Signing then is Heritage Tenant.

If you hold out, Gordie tells you they've bought every note on Main Street and thirteen businesses have signed; only you and Lionel haven't, and they want your shop very badly (§{salGordie}). In the Town Hall vault (§{salVault}) your 1887 deed holds a right of way to the harbor through your cellar, "forever", which the plan can't do without, and the fourteen "partnership agreements" all transfer to shell companies at one Boston address.

At the zoning hearing (§{salHearing}) read out the deed and the shells, and Saltire goes into receivership and your installments are suspended (Receivership). Refuse to sign and the plan is tabled (Holdout). Or sign in front of everyone (Heritage Tenant). Lionel redeems his watch unless you signed (§{salShattuckSigned}).

shattuckWatch.name: Silver pocket watch, engraved "A.S. 1951"
tells: Inside the lid: "Amos Shattuck, Shoe Repair, 1951. Heels while you wait."
Lionel winds it every morning at the bench, his father did, and his grandfather. It has never once stopped.

salShattuck.title: Lionel Shattuck, the cobbler, and his father's watch

steps.text: Lionel Shattuck, three doors down. Shoes, keys, the odd zipper. I've walked past your aunt's window every morning for forty years and never once come in.

steps.narrate: He sets a silver pocket watch on the glass and keeps two fingers on it.

steps.text: A company in Boston bought my mortgage off the bank. Saltire Capital. The payments doubled. I hear they bought your aunt's paper too, so you know the letterhead.

choose.label: "Keep it, Lionel. I'll not take your father's watch."

then.why: Lent $70 to Lionel Shattuck against his father's watch

then.text: I'll be back for it. Don't wind it. It doesn't like strangers.

else.text: Then I'll sell my good bench to Gordie Haines, and fix shoes on the old one.

steps.text: There was a woman in my shop yesterday with a folder. Very nice. Very sorry about the payments. She'll be in to see you.
Imogen Thackeray, community partnerships, Saltire Capital. Please don't look at me like Ms. Vantreece. We bought her paper, not her manners.

steps.narrate: She opens a folder on the counter: a drawing of Main Street with the clapboard fronts gone, and glass, and the words HARBORSIDE COMMONS.

text: Main Street, reimagined. Shops on the ground floor, condos above, a harbor walk. Every business that partners with us stays, rent-free for a year, as a heritage tenant.
Sign the partnership and your installments stop today. All of them, for as long as you stay. When the lease is up, the building comes to us. That's all.

choose.label: Sign the partnership
choose.hint: (no more installments; the building goes to Saltire)

then.text: Wonderful. You're the fourteenth. Only the cobbler left.

then.narrate: The installment line on your calendar goes grey.

then.text: Please do. The zoning hearing's the last week of the month. It would be lovely to have you with us by then.
Of course. The hearing's the last week of the month. The offer stands until the vote.

salGordie.title: Gordie Haines on who Saltire has bought

text: Your Saltire lady bought me lunch. She doesn't want my lot, she wants my opinion. I've never been so frightened.
Here's my opinion. They bought every note on Main Street, all through the autumn. Every business that's behind gets a letter, then a visit, then a folder.
They need every lot signed before the zoning hearing, or the board won't look at it. Thirteen have signed. Not you, not Lionel Shattuck.
And ask yourself why they want a pawnshop so badly. Nobody wants a pawnshop that badly. Your aunt never let me see her deeds. Marguerite has the town's copy.

steps.toast: Calendar: the Town Hall vault, {placed:sal-vault} night

salVault.title: The deeds in the Town Hall vault

steps.narrate: Under the Town Hall meeting room: a round steel door standing open, annual reports back to 1854, one bulb on a chain.

steps.text: I am not supposed to let shopkeepers in here after six. I am also the moderator of Town Meeting, so I decide what I'm supposed to do.
Marguerite gave me the key. I'm told I'm a "safe pair of hands". I've been called worse.

steps.narrate: The clerk lets you in, yawns, and leaves you with the bulb.

narrate: The deed for 14 Main Street, The Crooked Scale, 1887. A clause in copperplate: "a right of way, six feet wide, from Main Street to the harbor, through the cellar, for the landing of goods, forever."
Every plan for Harborside Commons needs the harbor walk. The harbor walk needs your cellar. Without your signature there's no Commons at all.
In the box beside it, filed this month: fourteen "partnership agreements". Each one is a deed of transfer with a nice cover sheet. Each one is to a different company with the same Boston address.

text.then: Fourteen shell companies. That is not a partnership, that is a magic trick. I'll put it on the hearing agenda, if you'll stand up and say it.
text.else: Fourteen companies, one mailbox. The town has seen this before, in 1887. That's why the clause says forever.

steps.toast: Calendar: the zoning hearing, Town Hall

salShattuckSigned.title: Lionel signs too, and doesn't want the watch back

steps.text: You signed. Everybody says so. Then I'll sign too; there's no Main Street with one cobbler on it.

then.text: Keep the watch. Give me forty more for it. I won't need a watch in a shop that's not mine.

salHearing.title: The zoning hearing for Harborside Commons

steps.narrate: The Town Hall meeting room, folding chairs and a coffee urn. The zoning board sits behind a table with a paper tablecloth. On an easel: HARBORSIDE COMMONS.

steps.text: Thirteen of fourteen Main Street businesses have chosen partnership. We ask the board to rezone, subject to the last signature, which we're confident of.

steps.narrate: {foe.vote.name} stands up to say Main Street could do with some glass.
{ally.vote.name} stands up to say the same thing about you that they say at the counter, only louder.

choose.label: Read out the 1887 right of way, and the fourteen companies at one address

then.narrate: The room goes quiet in the way only a New England room can. The chairman asks Ms. Thackeray which of the fourteen companies she works for. She says she'd have to check.

then.text: This is a misunderstanding. Saltire will be in touch.

then.narrate: Saltire isn't. By Friday the state has frozen its accounts, and a receiver writes to say your installments are suspended "pending review".

choose.label: "The Crooked Scale isn't signing. Not this month, not any month."

then.narrate: The board tables the rezoning "until all parties are in agreement". Ms. Thackeray smiles at you as if you've both agreed to have lunch.

then.why: Stood up to Saltire at the zoning hearing

choose.label: Sign, in front of everyone
choose.hint: (no more installments; the building goes to Saltire)

then.narrate: You sign on the paper tablecloth, because there's nowhere else. The board rezones Main Street by a vote of four to one. Lionel Shattuck signs after you, and doesn't look at you.

then.why: Signed Main Street over to Saltire

then.text: Keep the watch. Give me forty more for it. I won't need a watch in a shop that's not mine.

then.why: Lionel Shattuck redeemed his father's watch

then.text: I'll take my father's watch back now. It's a good day for it.

epilogue.line: Main Street is fenced off for Harborside Commons. The Crooked Scale is open behind the fence, with a sign the developers chose: "Heritage Pawnbroker, est. 1887".
Harborside Commons is tabled. Ms. Thackeray sends a card every month. The installments come every week.
Saltire Capital is in receivership, and fourteen Main Street businesses have their own deeds back. Lionel Shattuck fixed your shoes for free. He says it's once only. It is not once only.
